title: Cumulative dose evaluation in clinical reirradiation – Consensus guidance on technical considerations by the ESTRO reirradiation focus group
authors: Appelt AL, Andrzejewski P, Hoffmann L, et al.
scope: Cross-site technical guidance on cumulative (multi-course) dose evaluation / dose summation in reirradiation
notes: Not in Europe PMC full text (PMID 41318002, not OA there). Full text captured verbatim as rendered article innerText from publisher OA HTML (thegreenjournal.com) via the browser pane; tables are flattened (tab-separated). 35 Delphi consensus statements (Table 3). Key methods: (1) ALWAYS rescale to equieffective dose (EQD2Gy or BED) before any point or volumetric summation; multi-phase courses rescaled separately (CS11). (2) Suitable alpha/beta per normal tissue, consistent across all dose distributions for a tissue; when reRT-specific data lacking, use established primary-RT alpha/beta values and acknowledge uncertainty; evaluating multiple alpha/beta values helps assess uncertainty; where previous GTV is gone, use normal-tissue alpha/beta for all of the dose distribution; preferably map physical dose first then rescale to avoid alpha/beta discontinuities (CS12). (3) Recovery: if assumed, recovery factor applied to previously delivered EQUIEFFECTIVE dose, per structure; evidence sparse; DO NOT double-count recovery when published reRT constraints already implicitly assume recovery via minimum interval requirements (CS13). (4) No 3D summation of physical dose for quantitative OAR evaluation (CS14); physical sum underestimates where >2 Gy/fx, conservative where <2 Gy/fx in both courses. (5) Primary cumulative metric = near-maximum dose, defined for a very small volume e.g. D0.1cm3 rather than point/voxel (Table 1, CS16); volumetric metrics (mean, Vx) require full 3D equieffective summation and cannot be added from DVHs (CS17). (6) Without DICOM: manual near-max point summation (worst case); if only prescription known, default assumption OAR max = prescription dose unless technique known to give higher normal-tissue doses (e.g. old 2D/wedge). (7) Brachytherapy: sum equieffective near-max doses e.g. D2cm3, D1cm3 (CS23). (8) Proton/ion: verify whether doses are RBE-weighted or physical (CS21). (9) Document: previous treatments, dates, technique, delivered dose/fractionation, methodology, alpha/beta values, tissue recovery factors; templated reporting (CS32); communicate uncertainties (CS33). Methods A–H table (Table 2) ranks summation methods from max-point worst-case to robust voxel-wise accumulation.

title: Reirradiation Collaborative Group (ReCOG) consensus on standards for dose evaluation and reporting in patients with multiple courses of radiation therapy: an AAPM/ACRO/ASTRO/CARO/COMP/CADRA/CPQR/ESTRO/NRG-endorsed consensus statement
authors: Paradis KC, Appelt AL, Bentzen SM, et al.
scope: Cross-site standards for cumulative dose evaluation, documentation and reporting across multiple RT courses
notes: Paywalled (Lancet "Get Access"); not OA in Europe PMC (PMID 41643699). Abstract only: covers image-registration-based and point-dose-based dose accumulation, uncertainties in data availability, physiological organ recovery and anatomical change; abstract contains no numeric constraints. Quoted inside ESTRO 2025 guidance: image registration-based dose accumulation is usually the preferred method. A companion case-based guide exists (Pract Radiat Oncol 2026, doi 10.1016/j.prro.2026.03.012, not OA). No records extracted.

title: Clinical workflow for reirradiation: national consensus recommendations on imaging, treatment planning, dose accumulation, and treatment delivery
authors: Kaplan LP, Tobin RJ, Appelt A, et al.
scope: Danish national, site-independent consensus on reirradiation workflow, dose evaluation, QA of dose mapping, reporting and trials
notes: Key methods: dose must always be converted to equieffective dose before summation, each dose distribution rescaled individually (even if both prescriptions were 2 Gy/fx, OAR dose/fx differs); alpha/beta uncertain and endpoint-dependent; different worst-case alpha/beta values may be used for robust evaluation. Spinal cord alpha/beta 2 Gy widely used (values as low as 0.87 Gy published). No agreement on tissue recovery factor (TRF) or its time dependence for any OAR; some studies suggest >=6 months for 25% spinal cord recovery; recovery data lacking for heart, vessels, bronchi, oesophagus, lungs. Simple conservative planning: custom near-max constraint (e.g. D2%) from previous near-max dose (often overestimates). Reporting: cumulative near-maximum equieffective critical OAR doses (e.g. D2%) in patient chart; DVH parameters if 3D accumulation performed; registration uncertainties, alpha/beta values and TRFs. Table 1: DIR QA checklist (must/should/may). Table 2: evaluation scenarios A–I by feasibility x criticality (e.g. G: patient records only + high-dose overlap in critical OAR -> estimate max point dose with equieffective correction based on prescribed dose). Delivered-dose evaluation at least weekly (conventional) and daily (stereotactic). Supports ESTRO-EORTC type 1/type 2 reRT definitions. No organ dose thresholds given.

title: ESTRO/EANO recommendation on reirradiation of glioblastoma
authors: Andratschke N, Heusel A, Albert NL, et al.
license: Open access (publisher OA HTML; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0)
scope: Recurrent glioblastoma reirradiation (patient selection, imaging, targets, dose, OAR assessment, follow-up)
notes: Not OA in Europe PMC (PMID 42928533). Captured verbatim as rendered OA HTML innerText (corrected online version). CORRIGENDUM (Radiother Oncol 218:111438, 2026; saved as sources/estro-eano-gbm-corrigendum.txt): the alpha/beta for the EQD2 36 Gy target prescription was corrected from 3 Gy to 10 Gy; the saved text already reads 10 Gy. The guideline gives NO numeric cumulative OAR dose limits. Recommendations: EQD2 preferred over BED/EUD for accumulation (rec 11; text says alpha/beta 3 Gy); recovery only consistently described for brain and spinal cord, so only consider recovery for these (rec 13); minimum OAR set: brain, brainstem, optic chiasm, optic nerves/tract, cranial nerves near PTV (statement 5); both methods valid for brain: same first-course constraints with first-course dose discount OR cumulative constraints (statement 6); considerable uncertainty about recovery of optic chiasm/nerves (statement 7); no consensus on recovery for brainstem/optic pathways. Rigid registration recommended for target definition and dose accumulation (rec 5). Interval > 6 months, KPS >= 60 (rec 2). PTV margin max 3 mm. Background (not recommendations): cord tolerance increases >=25% at 6 months; cited series (ref 17) with no relevant long-term toxicity at max EQD2 (alpha/beta 2) 80.3/79.4/95.2 Gy chiasm/optic nerves/brainstem.

title: Corrigendum to "ESTRO/EANO recommendation on reirradiation of glioblastoma" [Radiother. Oncol. 204 (2025) 110696]

authors: Biau J, Beddok A, Sharma M, et al.
scope: Recurrent/second primary HNSCC reirradiation: selection, imaging, delineation, planning, dose accumulation, toxicity
notes: eScholarship item page and PDF (qt4kq0x28z) are behind a proof-of-work bot-check (Techaro BotStopper); not bypassed per rules. Lancet version paywalled (abstract only, no numbers). title: Principles of reirradiation
authors: Harrow S, Sadozye A, King AP, et al. (The Royal College of Radiologists)
journal: The Royal College of Radiologists, London (Clinical Oncology guidance)
scope: UK cross-site principles for reirradiation (cited by Danish consensus and ESTRO guidance)
notes: Text extracted from PDF with pypdf (sentence-final periods render as a replacement character). Key methods: convert previous dose to BED or EQD2; manual calculations incl. choice of alpha/beta independently checked; record cumulative EQD2/BED with alpha/beta used; choice of alpha/beta guided by literature; document any recovery incorporated; recovery discount at clinician discretion (citing Paradis 2019); summed physical-dose plans inadequate (esp. SABR reRT); worst-case expansion of high-dose region; OAR cumulative dose usually prioritised over PTV coverage; ideally >= 6 months from completion of primary treatment; ECOG PS <= 2. No organ thresholds (defers to RCR site-specific consensus statements).

title: The Special Medical Physics Consult Process for Reirradiation Patients
authors: Paradis KC, Mayo C, Owen D, et al.
scope: University of Michigan cross-site institutional reirradiation physics consult workflow (cited by RCR, Danish consensus, ESTRO guidance)
notes: Institutional workflow paper. Methods: EQD2 per voxel, rigid registration only (no DIR), near-maximum DVH metrics (D0.1cc or D0.03cc) preferred over mean/volumetric metrics; max point dose from paper records when DICOM absent; composite plans with and without discount; remaining allowable dose returned in physical dose for the new fractionation. Limits and time-dependent discount factors in Appendix E2 (saved separately) reflect physician consensus and in-house experience, many not literature-based; authors note limits break down for high dose-per-fraction courses.

title: Appendix E2 (Special Medical Physics Consultation – Previous Treatment Evaluation form) to Paradis et al. 2019
authors: Paradis KC, Mayo C, Owen D, et al.
scope: Institutional cumulative EQD2 D0.1cc OAR limits and time-dependent prior-dose discount factors (all body sites)
notes: Form carries disclaimer: dosimetric guidelines not endorsed by University of Michigan for use outside UM; document provided for example only. PDF text via pypdf: the column header alpha/beta is rendered by the SymbolMT font as the characters "D", 0x12, "E" (glyph IDs offset 29 from Symbol codes a,/,b; verified via font inspection) — so "DE(Gy)" = alpha/beta (Gy) = 2.5 for every OAR. Column "Dose limit Max to 0.1cc (EQD2) (Gy)"; discount columns <3 mo, 3-6 mo, 6 mo-1 yr, 1-3 yrs; "For >3 years, 50% discount suggested". Liver/Lungs table uses columns <3 mo, 3-6 mo, 6 mo-2 yr, >2 yr. Kidneys ALARA, Liver "NTCP limited", Lungs "Customized per case" (no numeric limit). Discount applies to previous dose; limits are cumulative composite EQD2 (prior discounted + new).

title: Appendix E1 (worked examples) to Paradis et al. 2019
authors: Paradis KC, Mayo C, Owen D, et al.
scope: Two worked institutional reRT consult examples (pelvis; thoracic)
notes: States alpha/beta 2.5 Gy used for all biological corrections unless requested otherwise (conservative in most cases, reduces calculation errors). NOTE inconsistency: example 2 text says institutional lung discounts 25% for 6 mo–2 yr and 40% beyond 2 years, while Appendix E2 form lists Lungs >2 yr = 50%.

title: Applicability and usage of dose mapping/accumulation in radiotherapy
authors: Murr M, Brock KK, Fusella M, et al.
scope: General dose mapping/accumulation methodology (cited by ESTRO 2025 guidance)
notes: Methodological only: reRT mapping uncertainty is systematic for the second course; define intended use and ROI before choosing DMA workflow. No numeric constraints, alpha/beta or recovery values.

title: Comparative evaluation of dose accumulation strategies in the clinical reirradiation setting
authors: Solomou N, Serban M, Andrzejewski P, et al.
journal: Physics and Imaging in Radiation Oncology (doi 10.1016/j.phro.2026.100954)
scope: Companion to ESTRO 2025 guidance: applies methods to lung, head-and-neck and cervix brachytherapy reRT cases
notes: Recovery applied as EQD2Gy x (1 - TRF) to previous equieffective dose before summation; a 25% TRF example (lung case). Point-based methods (prescription sum, DVH-metric sum, point dose) consistently overestimated cumulative OAR dose vs volumetric RIR/DIR methods; local point-dose method least prone to overestimation. alpha/beta values are those adopted from Hardcastle et al. multicentre study for comparability, not recommendations.

title: Temporally Corrected Dose Accumulation – Next Steps in the Biology of Reirradiation
authors: Gopalakrishnan V, Feng B, Somasundaram E, et al.
scope: Proposal for DICOM-based temporally corrected dose accumulation with decay ("dose forgiveness") models
notes: Not peer reviewed. Recovery models (linear, exponential, logarithmic, Gaussian, Jones & Hopewell primate CNS model) presented as equations in images only; constants not in text, so no numeric recovery model extracted. Numeric cord statements are secondary citations (Sahgal 2019 cord SBRT).
